newsitem.title: INDIA: India's TISCO ties up with Inland Steel.
newsitem.headline: India's TISCO ties up with Inland Steel.

text.p: India's largest private steelmaker Tata Iron and Steel Co (TISCO) on Tuesday tied up with Inland Steel Industries of the U.S. to establish a network of steel processing units across India.

Company officials said the two firms, 50:50 partners in the joint venture, will initially set up two service centres, one near TISCO's headquarters in the northern city of Jamshedpur and another at Pune, close to Bombay.

"This will give us an avenue downstream of our main activity," TISCO managing director J.J. Irani told a news conference. "Nowadays the customer is king and we see this as a better way of serving our customers."
The first phase will require an investment of $20 million, he said.

Alok Saha, the managing director of the new company, Tata-Ryerson Ltd., said operations would begin by the end of the year. Three more centres are to be established -- at Gopalpur in the eastern state of Orissa, Hosur in Karnataka and Delhi.
"The centres initially will process and distribute steel to such rapidly-growing industries as automobile, appliance, equipment and other engineering industries," TISCO said in a statement.

"In addition to offering cost-reduction opportunities for large industry, Tata-Ryerson will offer state-of-the-art information technology, along with processing and distribution services to manage the supply and distribution chains for smaller consumers," the statement added.
"At about $10 million for each centre, I suppose it could be $50 million," Irani said when asked the size of the total investment in the joint venture.
Tata-Ryerson aims to process a total of one million tonnes of steel annually by the end of the next five years, Saha said.
Irani said the minimum quantity of steel TISCO's customers could buy at present was 50 tonnes. By contrast, Ryerson's average order size is about 300 pounds.

"In the United States, as small manufacturers are developing, the service centres have become the main suppliers," said Robert Darnall, chairman of Inland Industries, which owns 87 percent of Ryerson Tull, Inc., the U.S.'s largest metals and industrial plastics materials management centre operation.
"We will add value for customers in terms of higher quality, more reliable deliveries, and less inventories they have to carry," Darnall added.
TISCO said more than 30 percent of steel is bought through service centres worldwide, but the corresponding figure for India is less than five percent.
Tata-Ryerson is determined to change all that, Saha said.

"Service facilities are very fragmented in this country. There are several units which do some of the operations but not all. We're trying to consolidate that effort and provide it to the consumer," Saha added.

Chicago-based Inland Steel Industries, Inc., is a steel manufacturing, materials management, logistics and technical services company with 1996 sales of $4.6 billion. Tata Steel's net profits in 1995/96 were $157.74 million.
